_comment: Pre-registered per-fault QC panel for Train Ticket (the TT analogue of faults/verification_targets.json). For each fault, the Prometheus signal(s) that MUST move if the injection took effect; verify_injection.py scores baseline vs injection windows -> confirmed|borderline|unconfirmed. One canonical=true per fault drives the verdict. These are QC gates, NOT the study's modality claims. | 5 Sept 2026: nine new fault families added, thresholds MEASURED on stratatrace-tt with faults/measure_targets.sh. dns_delay is NOT here on purpose: six TT containers instrumented with a counting rule sent zero DNS packets across 600 requests, because Train Ticket resolves peers through Nacos over HTTP. The family is excluded from this application's matrix.
_metric_naming: TT services expose NO app-level request-duration metrics (no micrometer/actuator - see prometheus-tt.yml), so every signal here is cAdvisor (per-container CPU/mem/net) or node-exporter (host). cAdvisor 'name' label = the container name: services = 'trainticket_ts-<svc>-service_1' (match '.*ts-<svc>-service_1$'); the shared DB = 'mysql' (exact); noisy neighbor = '.*noisy-neighbor.*'. Consequence: latency-type faults (slow_db, svc_net, anomaly_net) have NO direct app-metric signal on TT - they verify via a closed-loop THROUGHPUT drop and are metrics-WEAK by design (the study's point: kernel/traces + the client-side load CSV carry them). Thresholds marked CALIBRATE are provisional pending VM calibration.

_windows._note: INJECTION_S >= 120 so a settled segment remains after the 1m-rate ramp.

_calibration: Calibrated 2026-08-04 on the VM under 15-user load (30s windows; the campaign uses 60s baseline / 120s injection which settle better). KEY FINDING: TT's latency-type faults are METRICS-BLIND - slow_db (search 60ms->28.8s), svc_net (65ms->2.96s), dependency_outage (37ms->30s hang), svc_cpu_cap-aggressive (63ms->163ms) show HUGE client latency but their cAdvisor CPU/network signals are weak or DIRECTION-FLIP with load (mysql CPU rose, not fell, once real query concurrency piled up behind the toxic). This is the study's thesis, not a bug: the kernel (blocked socket reads) + the load-CSV client latency carry these faults, not resource metrics -> expect these to verify BORDERLINE/unconfirmed. RELIABLE (verify confirmed): svc_mem_cap (limit->120MB), noisy_neighbor (fires + KPIs flat), dependency_outage seat-CPU->0 (needs the 120s window). SAFETY: anomaly_mem FRAC bounded to 35 in run_campaign_tt (default 88 near-OOMs TT's 33GB-baseline box). TO WATCH in the campaign: anomaly_cpu (30s window showed 66%->59%, likely a lull under the already-loaded box - the 120s window should saturate) and anomaly_net (barely moved KPI 73ms->78ms - the host-bridge netem may not be hitting TT's docker network; verify the target interface).

slow_db_mysql.name: mysql_cpu_throughput_drop
slow_db_mysql.why: CALIBRATE. Latency toxic on the shared mysql proxy: in the closed loop fewer queries/s complete -> mysql does less work/s -> CPU drops. METRICS-WEAK & a trace BLIND SPOT (mysql uninstrumented); the real signal is the KERNEL (services blocked in read() on the DB socket) + the client-side latency in the load CSV. Mirrors slow_db_catalogue on Sock Shop but starker (no app latency metric at all).

error_storm_mysql.name: mysql_net_recv_drop
error_storm_mysql.why: CALIBRATE. timeout/reset_peer toxic breaks DB connections -> fewer successful queries reach mysql -> inbound bytes drop. The primary error signal (5xx to clients) lives in the LOAD CSV + service LOGS, not Prometheus (no app metrics).

svc_cpu_cap_ts-travel-service.name: travel_cpu_usage_capped
svc_cpu_cap_ts-travel-service.why: CALIBRATE. cgroup quota pins ts-travel-service CPU at/below the cap (0.5 subtle / 0.2 aggressive). Reliable cAdvisor signal (same mechanism as Sock Shop svc_cpu_cap_carts). App-latency inflation is trace/kernel-visible but has no TT Prometheus metric.

svc_mem_cap_ts-order-service.name: order_memory_limit_dropped
svc_mem_cap_ts-order-service.why: The cap is applied: the limit drops from host-total to the cap (<= a few hundred MB). Reliable for both intensities (same as Sock Shop svc_mem_cap_carts).

svc_mem_cap_ts-order-service.name: order_oom_kills
svc_mem_cap_ts-order-service.why: an aggressive cap below the JVM working set forces OOM kills; subtle causes GC pressure without necessarily OOMing. CALIBRATE the cap vs the Spring Boot heap.

svc_net_ts-basic-service.name: basic_net_throughput_drop
svc_net_ts-basic-service.why: CALIBRATE. per-netns netem inside ts-basic-service inflates its hop latency -> in the closed loop it completes fewer aggregations/s -> transmit bytes drop. METRICS-WEAK (no app latency); traces/kernel carry the latency.

dependency_outage_ts-seat-service.name: seat_cpu_drops_to_zero
dependency_outage_ts-seat-service.why: docker pause FREEZES ts-seat-service -> its CPU goes to ~0. Reliable. But the CALLER-side impact (travel/preserve threads blocked on the frozen seat socket) is metrics/logs-INVISIBLE - a frozen dependency is exactly the kernel-wins case (blocked read() on the seat socket), same finding as Sock Shop dependency_outage.

noisy_neighbor.name: neighbor_cpu_active
noisy_neighbor.why: CALIBRATED 2026-08-04: subtle neighbor consumes ~0.30 core (threshold 0.15 fires) while TT search latency stays flat (55.6ms->59.1ms, +6%) - the KPIs-barely-move premise HOLDS for TT (the study finding, not a QC gate). The kernel-only showcase: host CPU contention is kernel-visible but TT-metric-blind.

anomaly_cpu.name: host_cpu_nonidle
anomaly_cpu.why:
MEASURED 5 Sept on stratatrace-tt run r1: baseline 51.1% CPU with std 14.75, injection 97.3%, and 100% of injection samples above the 80% absolute threshold. It read `borderline` on sigma alone.
The 5-sigma gate is UNSATISFIABLE here, not merely strict: 51.1 + 5 x 14.75 = 124.9% CPU, and CPU stops at 100. Train Ticket runs 40 JVMs, so its idle CPU varies by +/-15 points where Sock Shop's barely moves - and sigma is delta divided by that noise, so the same real saturation scores far lower here. Lowered to 2.5 (measured 3.13), which is a reachable gate rather than a looser one.
host-wide stress-ng saturates all cores (node-exporter, app-agnostic - identical to Sock Shop).

anomaly_mem.name: host_major_page_faults
anomaly_mem.why:
MEASURED 5 Sept on tt_anomaly_mem_r1 during a real run: 7.7 -> 650/s, sigma 193, frac 1.0. Clean separation with the threshold sitting well above the loaded baseline and far below the injected value.
PROMOTED TO CANONICAL over the memory-available ratio, which cannot work on this machine - see below. It is also the better measurement: major faults are the CONSEQUENCE of memory pressure, the system going to disk for pages, rather than a level that has to be compared against a moving floor.

anomaly_mem.name: host_mem_available_drop
anomaly_mem.why:
MEASURED under load: baseline 0.1881, injection 0.0923.
I set this to 0.30 earlier today from a reading taken AT REST, where it was 0.4141. Under campaign load - 40 JVMs plus LTTng - the resting figure is meaningless: the real baseline is 0.1881, already below 0.30, so the check was vacuous for the second time in one day. An IDLE BASELINE IS NOT A RUN BASELINE, and every threshold in this file has to be derived from a measurement taken while the collection is running.
0.13 sits below the loaded baseline and above the injected value. Corroborating only, because a level compared against a floor that moves with load is inherently fragile here - the page-fault rate is not.

anomaly_disk.name: host_disk_write_ops
anomaly_disk.why:
MEASURED 5 Sept on tt_anomaly_disk_r1, this machine, during a real run: 1563 -> 2950 writes/s (1.89x), baseline std 830.
The Sock Shop threshold of 1200 sits BELOW Train Ticket's resting 1563, so it scored frac=1.0 with nothing injected - it would have passed on coverage alone had sigma not held it back. A threshold carried between machines is a guess, and the dangerous direction is when the new machine's baseline already satisfies it. 2400 sits clearly above the resting value and below the injected mean.

anomaly_disk.name: host_disk_write_bytes
anomaly_disk.why: MEASURED: 175.8 -> 199.8 MB/s, only 1.14x, and the 90 MB threshold from Sock Shop is far below the 175.8 MB baseline. Corroborating only, because the effect here is genuinely small - see the note on the canonical target.

anomaly_disk.name: host_disk_queue_depth_NOT_A_TARGET
anomaly_disk.why:
MEASURED, and it moves the WRONG WAY on this machine: 65.7 -> 42.3. Kept with direction=decrease because that is what actually happens, and recorded rather than dropped because it is the most interesting number in this family.
Train Ticket's tracing writes ~176 MB/s of a disk that sustains 206, leaving ~30 MB/s of headroom - so stress-ng's direct+fsync writes add only ~24 MB/s here against ~80 MB/s on Sock Shop, and the synchronous writes appear to displace queued asynchronous ones rather than pile on top of them. The disk is already saturated by the collection before the fault starts.
That is the same lesson as the Sock Shop io_time finding, one step further: it is not only that BOUNDED metrics go blind, it is that on a busy enough application the fault itself has almost no room to act.

anomaly_net.name: anomaly_net_no_metric_signature
anomaly_net.why:
MADE UNSATISFIABLE ON PURPOSE - abs_threshold -1 on a byte rate that cannot go negative.
The first version of this known negative used direction=decrease with no absolute floor, and it ACCIDENTALLY PASSED: re-collected r1 and r2 were the same fault on the same 42 containers, and r1 read `confirmed` while r2 read `no_metric_signature`, purely because mysql's byte rate happened to drift down during r1's window.
`expected_to_fail` only takes effect when the check FAILS, so a target that can pass by chance still certifies by chance - the same false-positive route that put a zero-container run in the dataset earlier. A known negative has to be a check that cannot pass.

REGISTERED AS A KNOWN NEGATIVE, measured on tt_anomaly_net_r3 (42 containers, netem 80 ms delay / 20 ms jitter / 2% loss). Nothing in Prometheus moves:
  tcp retransmits            0 -> 0        host netstat cannot see container netns
  tcp out segments           2 -> 2        same reason
  container tcp sockets      306.8 -> 302.9   0.99x
  tx/rx packets dropped      0 -> 0        netem drops in the qdisc, not the iface
  gateway recv bytes         1456 -> 1539  1.06x

The reason is structural rather than a missing threshold. netem adds LATENCY, and Sock Shop's target for this family is application latency - histogram_quantile(0.95, http_request_duration_seconds_bucket) - which its services expose and Train Ticket's do not. The same fault is metrics-visible on one application and metrics-invisible on the other because of how the applications are instrumented, not because of anything about the fault.

THE PREVIOUS TARGET PRODUCED A FALSE POSITIVE. It was mysql's receive-byte rate with direction=decrease, and mysql's inbound traffic drifts with load: run r2, which injected into ZERO containers, was certified `confirmed` on a 1665 -> 864 drop with frac=1.0 and sigma=-3.09. A target that moves on its own can confirm a fault that never happened, which is the one outcome worse than confirming nothing.

The fault IS observable here - just not in this modality. The load generator's CSV records per-request latency, so the effect is in the dataset; it is the metrics modality that is blind, which is precisely the kind of claim the ablation study exists to make.

lock_contention.name: lock_contention_threads
lock_contention.why: MEASURED 5 Sept on stratatrace-tt: 17 threads, series absent before injection.

deadlock.name: deadlock_threads
deadlock.why: MEASURED: 25 threads. CPU is deliberately not a target - it reads 0.0001, because deadlocked threads consume nothing. A stuck system looks like an idle one.

fd_exhaustion.name: gateway_fd_ceiling
fd_exhaustion.why: MEASURED: 305 descriptors in use, capped, count fell to 257. No abs_threshold - the gateway idles at 175 where Sock Shop's Node front-end idles at 21, so only direction and sigma are portable between the two applications.

conn_pool_exhaustion.name: mysql_sockets_held
conn_pool_exhaustion.why: MEASURED 5 Sept: 204 -> 2005 sockets (9.8x) on the SHARED mysql. Train Ticket's 20 DB services all use this one server, so the blast radius here is far larger than Sock Shop's per-service database - a property of the applications, not of the recipe.

data_exfiltration.name: exfil_bytes_out
data_exfiltration.why: MEASURED 5 Sept: 42.0 MB/s. Read 0.0000 until the recipe was changed to send to a separate sink container instead of 127.0.0.1 inside its own.

data_exfiltration.name: exfil_bytes_in_at_sink
data_exfiltration.why: MEASURED: 42.0 MB/s at the receiving end.

fork_storm.name: fork_storm_processes
fork_storm.why: MEASURED: 201 processes. Per-container is ESSENTIAL here: node_forks_total measured only 1.05x in one pass and 7.2x in another, because Train Ticket already forks ~112/s from 40 JVMs and Nacos health checks. The storm disappears into the host baseline.

fork_storm.name: host_fork_rate
fork_storm.why: MEASURED: 15.7 -> 113.1/s (7.2x), but 112.7 -> 117.9 (1.05x) in an earlier pass. Corroborating only - it is not reliable on this application.

nagle_delayed_ack.name: nagle_workload_present
nagle_delayed_ack.why: MEASURED: 1.00 cores. A PRESENCE check only. The fault's signature - a ~99 ms stall clustered within 1 ms of itself against a TCP_NODELAY control at 0.51 ms in the same run - is invisible to every metric we collect, which is why the family exists.
